To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the foaming properties of pea and fababean protein concentrates are better than their isolates.

the foaming properties of pea and fababean protein concentrates and isolats are improved significantly by complexation with XG and controlling the intermolecular interactions between proteins and XG as a function of solution pH.
the foam stability of pulse protein concentrate and isolates was improved by the addition of Xanthan gum and controlling the intermolecular interactions of protein polysaccharides at pH 5.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the utilization of pulse proteins for foam stabilization by complexation with xanthan gum.
the development of pulse protein foaming properties by complexation with XG.
the development of a sustainable, environmentally friendly and healthy food ingredient that could be used for the development of new products with improved nutritional and textural properties.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
pulse protein foams with XG at pH 5, 9 and 7 for pea protein concentrate and isolate respectively, can be used for food applications where foams are desired.

pulse protein foams are stabilized by the formation of protein-polysaccharide complexes, which are pH dependent and their size, structure, and stability can be manipulated by the addition of XG and pH.
pulse protein XG foaming behavior was influenced by pH and protein content, and foams prepared with pea protein concentrates were more stable than faba bean protein isolates.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the pulse proteins have potential for foam stabilization, however, they are not comparable with egg albumen.
the addition of XG and control of protein XG interactions at optimum pH can improve the foaming properties of pea and fababean protein concentrates and isolats.
the foaming behavior and stability of pulse proteins is strongly influenced by pH and the presence of XG, and that pulse protein XG foaming behavior is similar to that of whey protein.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of protein XG foaming systems can be an attractive alternative to animal protein foams in various food applications.
the pulse proteins can be used as a source of proteins for foam stabilization.
pulse protein concentrates and isolatestabilize foams when complexed with XG at pH 5, 6.5 and 9.
